topic: Gaussian-free residual-law identification of all interventions in confounded additive-noise SCMs under an exact intervention cover. For a known acyclic treatment DAG with X_i=f_i(X_Pa(i))+U_i and Y=f_Y(X)+U_Y, allow an arbitrary correlated Borel disturbance law with finite second moments. Given the full observational law, do(X=x), and a fixed finite regime collection R whose families leave each i free while intervening on all Pa(i), require coverage of the entire observational support and every recursively reached target support. Prove that regime means identify every structural mean, observational residuals identify the complete centered joint exogenous law, and a topological residual pushforward identifies every covered postintervention distribution and bounded AOI. Prove the same exact combinatorial cover is necessary for universal identification by two bounded non-Gaussian SCMs that agree simultaneously on the complete regime tuple but differ on a target intervention. Construct a cross-fitted regime-regression plus joint-residual-resampling estimator with bootstrap inference for smooth AOIs and distributional bands under explicit no-atom/density conditions. Use the four-point Rademacher residual witness and Jeunen et al.'s published International Stroke Trial semi-synthetic intervention-disentanglement benchmark; do not claim a new clinical aspirin conclusion.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the parent-intervention cover that is necessary and sufficient for Gaussian average outcomes also identify every covered postintervention distribution in a known-DAG confounded additive-noise SCM with an arbitrary centered Borel joint disturbance law, and is that same cover universally necessary?

source_refs.claim: The published result gives necessary and sufficient intervention-cover conditions for all average outcomes but assumes multivariate Gaussian disturbances.
source_refs.author: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Mahsa Ghasemi, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies single-intervention mean effects from joint regimes using additive multivariate Gaussian noise and names removal of Gaussianity as future work.
source_refs.author: Olivier Jeunen, Ciarán M. Gilligan-Lee, Rishabh Mehrotra, Mounia Lalmas

source_refs.excerpt: The lower family uses O(log T) latent states and therefore says nothing about a uniformly bounded latent alphabet.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest intervention-cover results use Gaussian conditional-expectation and covariance identities, which recover mean effects but neither an arbitrary dependent disturbance law nor a complete postintervention distribution. A Gaussian-free argument must instead identify each structural mean from parent-fixing regimes, recover the entire centered residual vector from the observational law, and prove uniqueness of its recursive pushforward. Universal necessity adds a separate construction obstacle: two bounded non-Gaussian SCMs must match the complete observational-plus-regime tuple simultaneously while differing at one uncovered target. The prior lower-bound attempt documents the analogous difficulty of compressing an indistinguishability construction to fixed support; here growing latent coding must be replaced by a four-point signed perturbation whose cancellations survive every supplied regime.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient identification theorem giving an explicit regime-mean and joint-residual pushforward formula for every covered intervention law and bounded AOI, together with fixed four-point bounded non-Gaussian two-SCM witnesses whenever the cover fails.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation, formal intervention-family setup, and exact cover language are the closest framing, while its Gaussian and mean-level boundaries expose the destination clearly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: All intervention combinations are scientifically relevant but exponentially numerous -> confounded ANM structure lets a small parent-cover recover Gaussian AOIs -> determine whether the same cover recovers complete intervention laws without Gaussianity

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the nodewise parent-cover induction and necessity construction, replacing Gaussian covariance recovery with structural-mean identification and recovery of the complete residual vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It proves the exact average-outcome analogue under essentially the same regime combinatorics.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the multi-regime disentanglement argument while replacing its Gaussian conditional-noise calculation with a residual-law pushforward.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest published nonlinear confounded-ANM result and explicitly identifies non-Gaussianity as an unresolved boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its functional delta method, joint empirical-process limit, and exchangeable bootstrap for plug-in counterfactual distribution operators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once residual pushforward identifies an intervention CDF, the estimation target is a generated counterfactual distribution process rather than only a scalar mean.

open_problems.open_problem: Can cross-fitted regime regressions and joint residual resampling deliver asymptotically linear smooth-AOI estimators and valid simultaneous bootstrap bands for intervention CDFs in non-Gaussian confounded additive-noise SCMs?

source_refs.claim: The pooled multi-regime estimator is evaluated empirically under Gaussian noise without a functional CLT or uniform distributional inference theory.
source_refs.author: Olivier Jeunen, Ciarán M. Gilligan-Lee, Rishabh Mehrotra, Mounia Lalmas

source_refs.claim: This paper proves functional CLTs and bootstrap validity for regression-based counterfactual distributions, but not for multi-regime generated residual laws in confounded SCMs.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Iván Fernández-Val, Blaise Melly

source_refs.excerpt: no primitive learner class, rate derivation, or attainable example discharges it

open_problems.why_unsolved: The residual empirical law is formed from estimated structural functions shared across regimes, so ordinary plug-in arguments must control generated residuals, unequal regime sample sizes, and repeated propagation of each estimated disturbance vector through a recursive intervention map. Smooth AOIs require an influence expansion containing both regression and residual-law terms, while CDF bands introduce a nonsmooth indicator process whose equicontinuity can fail at atoms. The prior review identifies the recurring proof defect directly: imposing a high-level distributional convergence rate is insufficient without a primitive learner class and attainable rate derivation. Existing DML theory lacks the recursive residual pushforward, while counterfactual-distribution theory does not cover this confounded multi-regime generated-regressor structure.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator-and-limit theorem specifying primitive learner and nuisance-rate conditions, an influence function and root-n limit for smooth AOIs, and a valid multiplier or exchangeable bootstrap in sup norm for intervention CDFs under explicit density and no-atom conditions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its estimation section and International Stroke Trial semi-synthetic benchmark frame the finite-regime data-fusion problem whose uncertainty quantification remains undeveloped.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational and joint-intervention samples can disentangle unseen interventions -> practical use requires learning nonlinear mechanisms from finite regime samples -> valid uncertainty must include regression and reconstructed-noise error

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a Neyman-orthogonal score for a smooth pushforward AOI and use cross-fitting to make first-stage regression errors enter through product-rate remainders.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target is low-dimensional but depends on flexible regime-specific structural regressions, matching the nuisance configuration addressed by DML.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the Hadamard differentiability calculation for counterfactual distribution operators and its exchangeable-bootstrap functional CLT.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired distributional result is a simultaneous band for a counterfactual CDF indexed by thresholds.

open_problems.open_problem: When a regime collection misses part of a recursively reached parent support, what are the sharp identified bounds on postintervention distributions and bounded AOIs under explicit Lipschitz, monotonicity, or directional-derivative restrictions on the uncovered structural mechanisms?

source_refs.claim: The point-identification argument requires regimes exposing every node while its parents are intervened upon and does not characterize the identified set when required parent values are unsupported.
source_refs.author: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Mahsa Ghasemi, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: The paper derives nonparametric extrapolation bounds under directional-derivative restrictions, but not recursively propagated causal-SCM bounds.
source_refs.author: Niklas Pfister, Peter Bühlmann

open_problems.why_unsolved: At the first uncovered parent value, no regime mean determines the corresponding structural function, and each descendant intervention law depends recursively on that free value. Standard lack-of-overlap bounds concern one regression or potential-outcome margin; here admissible extrapolations at several nodes are coupled through a common joint residual law and a topological composition. Sharpness therefore requires globally compatible extremal mechanisms across the DAG rather than independently propagated nodewise intervals.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-set characterization, with constructive extremizing SCMs, for intervention CDFs and bounded AOIs under stated shape restrictions, collapsing to the residual-pushforward singleton exactly when recursive support coverage holds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing separates interpolation from unsupported extrapolation and motivates transparent bounds instead of silent regression extension.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Nonparametric conditional functions are learned only on observed support -> intervention recursion can request values outside that support -> encode extrapolation restrictions and report bounds for the resulting causal law

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate directional-derivative envelopes for each uncovered structural regression through the SCM recursion while enforcing compatibility with the common residual law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its lower and upper extrapolation operators address the first unidentified object: the off-support structural mean.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent AOI endpoints as intersection bounds and adapt bias correction, Gaussian-process approximation, and adaptive inequality selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Recursive shape-constrained envelopes generate families of upper and lower restrictions whose extrema define the identified region.

open_problems.open_problem: Which nested and conditional counterfactual distributions become identifiable from an exact intervention cover in a confounded additive-noise SCM because the observational residual vector supplies a common cross-world disturbance coupling, even when unrestricted graph-only counterfactual identification fails?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives complete graph-based identification of nested and conditional counterfactuals from observational and experimental distributions and shows that cross-world factors can remain unidentified.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Sanghack Lee, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The intervention-cover theorem identifies average interventional outcomes, not joint cross-world or factual-conditioned counterfactual laws.
source_refs.author: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Mahsa Ghasemi, Murat Kocaoglu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Interventional marginals generally do not determine how the same unit's outcomes are coupled across worlds, which is why unrestricted graphical counterfactual identification can fail. In an additive SCM with cover-identified structural functions, however, the observational residual map may reveal the joint exogenous vector reused in every world. The missing proof step is to establish that regular conditional laws of this residual vector given factual events are uniquely determined and evaluable along every nested support recursion. The located literature does not combine counterfactual factorization with mechanism and residual-law recovery from a confounded-ANM intervention cover.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient residual-cover characterization and explicit abduction-action-prediction functional for marginal and factual-conditioned nested counterfactual distributions, with counterexamples at failed cover or conditional-support fibers.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the causal-ladder motivation, precise nested-query notation, and examples where arbitrary experiments still leave cross-world factors unidentified.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observational and experimental data live below the counterfactual layer -> nested queries require a common cross-world coupling -> test whether identified additive residuals provide that missing coupling

method_exemplars.technique: Apply counterfactual unnesting and counterfactual-factor decomposition, replacing otherwise unidentified cross-world factors by pushforwards of the common recovered residual vector.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its factorization precisely locates the cross-world objects that residual recovery may newly identify.

method_exemplars.technique: Extend nodewise parent-cover recovery from average outcomes to complete structural functions before performing SCM abduction and recursive action.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the intervention-cover mechanism recovery absent from graph-only counterfactual calculus.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt functional empirical-process and bootstrap arguments to estimated conditional pushforwards of the recovered residual distribution.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The estimation target is again a function-valued counterfactual distribution, now with an additional factual-conditioning operator.

open_problems.open_problem: What necessary-and-sufficient analogue of a parent intervention cover identifies full postintervention laws when the available regimes are known soft or stochastic mechanism changes rather than surgical parent-fixing interventions?

source_refs.claim: The paper gives graphical identification and transportability criteria for soft interventions but does not exploit additive structure to recover mechanisms and a dependent residual law.
source_refs.author: Juan D. Correa, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The paper characterizes latent-variable graph equivalence under controlled soft interventions, targeting structure rather than full effect-law recovery.
source_refs.author: Murat Kocaoglu, Amin Jaber, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: The confounded-ANM cover theorem is formulated for hard interventions exposing a node while all of its parents are intervened upon.
source_refs.author: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Mahsa Ghasemi, Murat Kocaoglu

open_problems.why_unsolved: A hard parent intervention makes a regime mean directly expose a structural function up to a common disturbance location. A soft intervention generally retains parental variation and may alter the node disturbance, invalidating that first proof step. Graphical soft-intervention calculus can decide recoverability in unrestricted models, but it does not characterize when several known mechanism changes are algebraically rich enough to invert the additive structural functions and reconstruct the baseline cross-node disturbance coupling. The located soft-intervention and confounded-ANM papers provide no exact full-law functional cover for this setting.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A graphical-algebraic rank or correspondence condition on the soft-regime family that is necessary and sufficient for an explicit baseline-mechanism and residual-law recovery functional, with a matching two-model failure witness.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation explains why real interventions are often stochastic mechanism modifications and distinguishes available input regimes from target interventions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Experiments rarely implement atomic do operations -> soft interventions require their own identification calculus -> exploit additive-noise structure to turn known soft shifts into an exact full-law cover

method_exemplars.technique: Use sigma-calculus reductions and augmented regime nodes to isolate which baseline causal factors can be replaced by known soft kernels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a complete language for distinguishing available soft regimes from the desired target intervention.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize the hard parent-cover induction by replacing direct mean revelation with an invertible system of regime-contrast equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its theorem identifies the hard-intervention endpoint to which a soft-cover condition should reduce.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt invariant-prediction confidence sets across noise-shift environments to test the regime correspondences required by the recovery map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies inference procedures built specifically from mechanism-changing environments.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one jointly recover the treatment DAG, all structural mechanisms, and the complete dependent disturbance law from a polylogarithmic intervention design when additive disturbances are non-Gaussian and mutually dependent?

source_refs.claim: The paper jointly recovers the observable graph and all average outcomes with polylogarithmically many interventions, but under multivariate Gaussian noise and faithfulness.
source_refs.author: Muhammad Qasim Elahi, Mahsa Ghasemi, Murat Kocaoglu

source_refs.claim: NoGAM recovers a topological order under arbitrary noise distributions, but its score factorization and residual argument require mutually independent node noises.
source_refs.author: Francesco Montagna, Nicoletta Noceti, Lorenzo Rosasco, Kun Zhang, Francesco Locatello
source_refs.venue: Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning

source_refs.claim: The randomized latent-variable intervention design learns observable structure in O(d log-squared n) experiments but does not recover nonlinear structural functions or a joint exogenous law.
source_refs.author: Murat Kocaoglu, Karthikeyan Shanmugam, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: Arbitrary-noise observational ANM discovery uses a score identity whose density factorization fails under correlated disturbances. Conversely, latent-confounding intervention designs recover edge information from separation changes but do not identify nonlinear functions or the full cross-node disturbance coupling. The missing first step is a regime contrast that orients candidate parent relations without Gaussian covariance algebra or residual independence while ensuring that the selected regimes form a mechanism-identifying cover.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint recovery theorem and algorithm specifying an intervention design, a graph-and-mechanism recovery map, its success probability or sample complexity, and a nonidentifiability frontier when dependent-noise orientation conditions fail.

writing_exemplar.why: It combines intervention selection, graph recovery, and effect identification, making the arbitrary-dependent-noise boundary easy to state.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The graph required for effect identification may itself be unknown -> randomized interventions can jointly learn Gaussian structure and collect an AOI cover -> seek the same economy while recovering nonlinear mechanisms and dependent non-Gaussian residuals

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the separating-system randomized intervention design and its high-probability edge-exposure argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the combinatorial machinery behind the published polylogarithmic Gaussian design.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt score-versus-residual dimension reduction for leaf detection, replacing independence factorization with invariances across parent-fixing regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest generic-noise mechanism for extracting a topological order, and its failed independence step identifies what interventions must repair.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its intervention-aware minimax analysis and two-step penalized estimation argument to separate design error from mechanism-estimation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a template for proving rates under chosen interventions rather than stopping at population identifiability.

literature_map:
Jeunen et al. (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2210.05446) identify single-intervention mean effects from joint regimes under additive multivariate Gaussian noise and explicitly leave non-Gaussian noise to future work.
Their International Stroke Trial experiment is semi-synthetic: treatment and outcome variables include simulated components and Gaussian confounding, so it is a methodological benchmark rather than new clinical evidence.
Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (TMLR 2025, arXiv:2407.10014) provide the closest theorem: parent-cover conditions are necessary and sufficient for all average outcomes in confounded Gaussian ANMs.
That TMLR result is mean-level and relies on Gaussian conditional expectations and covariance recovery; it does not identify arbitrary postintervention laws.
Saengkyongam and Silva (UAI 2020, arXiv:2005.11528) study the complementary direction—joint effects from singleton interventions—again with additive Gaussian noise.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) give sound and complete generalized identification from surrogate experiments without exploiting additive mechanisms or recovering a joint exogenous law.
Kandasamy, Bhattacharyya, and Honavar (AAAI 2019, DOI:10.1609/aaai.v33i01.33012876) formulate minimum intervention cover graphically; their cover differs from the functional parent-support cover needed here.
Kocaoglu, Shanmugam, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2017) obtain polylogarithmic designs for graph learning with latent variables but not joint nonlinear mechanism-and-residual recovery.
Peters et al. (JMLR 2014, arXiv:1309.6779), Park (JMLR 2020), and Montagna et al. (CLeaR 2023, arXiv:2304.03265) develop arbitrary-noise ANM discovery under independent errors; correlated disturbances break their factorization.
Kocaoglu et al. (NeurIPS 2019) and Correa and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2020) characterize soft-intervention equivalence and transportability, but not an additive-noise full-law intervention cover.
Chernozhukov et al. (Econometrics Journal 2018, arXiv:1608.00060) supply cross-fitting and orthogonal-score machinery, while the closest confounded-ANM papers lack comparable asymptotic inference results.
Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Melly (Econometrica 2013, arXiv:0904.0951) provide the closest functional-CLT and bootstrap template for complete counterfactual distributions.
Pfister and Bühlmann (JMLR 2026, arXiv:2402.09758) formalize nonparametric extrapolation bounds, exposing a partial-identification route when recursive parent-support coverage fails.
Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2021, arXiv:2107.03190) give complete nested-counterfactual identification from surrogate experiments; a recovered common residual vector may identify cross-world factors unavailable in their unrestricted graphical model.
prior_proposal_map:
The active panel_ipcw_spectral_ssc_inference reviewer files were mined; review_math.json supplied a primitive-rate objection relevant to residual-process bootstrap theory.
The same review's support-transport finding exposed a distinction between combinatorial cover and recursive support propagation, but it was not retained as a separate opportunity after quality filtering.
The stat_pomdp_latent_overlap_minimax proto-core attempt was inspected; its honest_scope records a fixed-alphabet limitation relevant to compressing universal indistinguishability witnesses.
That attempt's uniform likelihood-factorization limitation was considered for approximate-cover minimax analysis but lacked enough direct topic support to survive filtering.
No angle-rejected proposal supplied a stronger confounded-ANM opportunity than the published Gaussian-cover boundary.
The retained prior-proposal evidence was cross-linked into the full-law identification and finite-sample inference opportunities rather than treated as an origin-based ranking bonus.
